title: The Hidden Plumbing of Stablecoins: Financial and Technological Risks in the GENIUS Act Era
summary: This paper evaluates financial, technological, and regulatory risks of GENIUS Act-compliant stablecoins as they scale into mainstream payment and settlement use. The authors argue that maintaining par-value redemption depends not only on backing-asset quality but also on Treasury and repo market functioning, broker-dealer balance-sheet capacity, and blockchain transaction rail reliability. Even conservatively backed stablecoins may face stress during redemption surges, market-intermediation bottlenecks, or technological disruptions.
key_points: The GENIUS Act (enacted 2025) established the first comprehensive U.S. federal framework for stablecoin issuance, backing, and supervision.

Stablecoin par-value stability depends on: backing-asset quality, Treasury market functioning, repo market functioning, broker-dealer balance-sheet capacity, and blockchain transaction rail reliability.
Conservative backing alone does not guarantee stability under stress scenarios.
Potential stress sources include: redemption surges, market-intermediation bottlenecks, and technological disruptions.
The authors argue durable stability requires an integrated approach across financial-market infrastructure, prudential regulation, and software governance.
Analysis identifies principles relevant for regulators in other jurisdictions developing stablecoin regimes.
why_it_matters: This research highlights critical dependencies in stablecoin infrastructure that could affect payment system stability and financial market plumbing. If stablecoins scale into mainstream settlement, stress events could propagate through Treasury and repo markets, affecting broader financial market functioning. The paper bridges crypto-asset regulation with traditional market structure concerns.
